status_legend.verified: Directly measured in this study and matching the claim.
status_legend.consistent: Our measurement supports the claim but does not uniquely establish it.
status_legend.partially_verified: Some components are measured; others remain external or untested.
status_legend.external_only: Not tested here; relies on an operator, public report, or cited paper.
status_legend.contradicted: Our measurement conflicts with the claim.
status_legend.not_tested: No measurement and no adequate external source.

claims.claim: More than 11,000 Starlink objects are in orbit.
claims.measured: {{metrics.snapshots.nov2026.n|,}} objects in the 2026-11-23 CelesTrak GP snapshot; SATCAT contains {{metrics.satcat.total|,}}.
claims.notes: Counts are on-orbit objects, not historical launches.

claims.claim: Starlink is roughly two of every three active satellites.
claims.measured: {{metrics.active_catalog.starlink|,}} of {{metrics.active_catalog.total|,}} active catalog objects = {{metrics.active_catalog.share_pct|.2f}}%.
claims.notes: Active catalog is a separate 2026-11-23 snapshot; the numerator matches the Starlink GP count.

claims.claim: Orbital speed is about 27,000 km/h.
claims.measured: Median circular speed {{metrics.altitude.speed_median_kmh|,}} km/h from the snapshot's semi-major axes.
claims.notes: Circular approximation; individual elliptical speeds vary.

claims.claim: The orbital period is about 1.5 h, or roughly 15 orbits per day.
claims.measured: Median period {{metrics.altitude.period_median_min|.2f}} min = {{metrics.altitude.orbits_per_day|.2f}} orbits/day.
claims.notes: Keplerian period from the TLE semi-major axis.

claims.claim: The constellation operates near 500 km, roughly 70 times lower than GEO.
claims.measured: Median {{metrics.altitude.median_km|.1f}} km (p05 {{metrics.altitude.p05_km|.1f}}, p95 {{metrics.altitude.p95_km|.1f}}); {{metrics.altitude.pct_below_500|.2f}}% below 500 km; GEO/median = {{metrics.altitude.geo_to_median_ratio|.1f}}x.
claims.notes: The distribution is not a single 500 km shell; 2.05% of objects are at or above 500 km.

claims.claim: The constellation uses several inclination families and resolved altitude shells.
claims.measured: {{metrics.shells.n_families}} inclination families ({{metrics.shells.families|join}}), {{metrics.shells.n}} resolved shells; {{metrics.shells.n_assigned|,}} of {{metrics.snapshots.nov2026.n|,}} objects assigned ({{metrics.shells.coverage_pct|.2f}}%).
claims.notes: Shell detection uses 2 km altitude histogram peaks, a 25-object minimum, and a +/-8 km assignment window.

claims.claim: Four large operational shells dominate the November 2026 snapshot.
claims.measured: 43.0 deg / 483 km n={{metrics.shells.by_key.43_483.n|,}}; 53.1 deg / 463 km n={{metrics.shells.by_key.53p1_463.n|,}}; 70.0 deg / 475 km n={{metrics.shells.by_key.70_475.n|,}}; 97.4 deg / 465 km n={{metrics.shells.by_key.97p4_465.n|,}}.
claims.notes: These four shells account for most of the assigned population; smaller deployment shells remain.

claims.claim: A small but non-zero population sits at or above 500 km.
claims.measured: {{metrics.altitude.n_above_500}} objects ({{metrics.altitude.above_500_pct|.2f}}%): 500-515 km {{metrics.altitude.above_500_bands.500_515}}, 515-535 km {{metrics.altitude.above_500_bands.515_535}}, 535-560 km {{metrics.altitude.above_500_bands.535_560}}, >=560 km {{metrics.altitude.above_500_bands.560_plus}}.
claims.notes: The 230 objects are a mixture of the 70 deg 525 km shell and a small high-altitude tail; they do not overturn the 'about 500 km' statement.

claims.claim: The plane lattice is not a single clean Walker set.
claims.measured: Effective RAAN groups: 43 deg / 483 km {{metrics.planes.by_key.43_483.planes}} (spacing {{metrics.planes.by_key.43_483.spacing_median_deg|.2f}} deg, CV {{metrics.planes.by_key.43_483.spacing_cv|.2f}}); 53.1 deg / 463 km {{metrics.planes.by_key.53p1_463.planes}} ({{metrics.planes.by_key.53p1_463.spacing_median_deg|.2f}} deg, CV {{metrics.planes.by_key.53p1_463.spacing_cv|.2f}}); 70 deg / 475 km {{metrics.planes.by_key.70_475.planes}}; 97.4 deg / 465 km {{metrics.planes.by_key.97p4_465.planes}}.
claims.notes: Counts are effective RAAN clusters after J2 rectification, not design plane numbers. Mean-anomaly and twin metrics are contaminated where adjacent planes merge.

claims.claim: A GEO bent-pipe at 35,786 km has a four-leg radio path above 140,000 km and about 0.48 s of light time.
claims.measured: {{metrics.latency.geo_alt_km|,}} km altitude; 4 x nadir slant = {{metrics.latency.geo_4leg_km|,}} km; {{metrics.latency.geo_4leg_ms|.2f}} ms.
claims.notes: Vacuum light time only; no processing, queueing, or fiber.

claims.claim: Public figures put GEO service at 600 ms or more and Starlink US peak-hour latency near 25 ms, with a 20 ms goal.
claims.measured: Not measured; this study has no end-to-end RTT probe.
claims.notes: Operator and public-network figures repeated by the explainer. Our radio-only bounds are not comparable to these end-to-end numbers.

claims.claim: A 550 km LEO bent-pipe has a ~7 ms radio-only RTT; the 10-site simulation bounds are 6.1-6.5 ms.
claims.measured: Ideal 550 km: {{metrics.latency.leo550_4leg_km|,}} km / {{metrics.latency.leo550_4leg_ms|.2f}} ms; site medians lower {{metrics.service.median_rtt_lower_p50_ms|.2f}} ms, upper {{metrics.service.median_rtt_upper_p50_ms|.2f}} ms.
claims.notes: Gateway-at-nadir (lower) and gateway-at-user (upper) bounds; excludes fiber, processing, scheduling, weather, and load.

claims.claim: Sites see tens of Starlink satellites above a 25 deg elevation mask.
claims.measured: Median visible p50 {{metrics.service.median_visible_p50|.1f}}; site range {{metrics.service.visible_p50_range.0}}-{{metrics.service.visible_p50_range.1}}.
claims.notes: Ten sites, 24 h at 15 s, satellites between 400 and 600 km.

claims.claim: Best-satellite handovers occur on 15-30 s scales.
claims.measured: p50 median {{metrics.service.median_handover_interval_s|.1f}} s (range {{metrics.service.handover_p50_range_s.0}}-{{metrics.service.handover_p50_range_s.1}}); p90 median {{metrics.service.median_handover_p90_s|.1f}} s.
claims.notes: Geometric best-satellite model, not the operational scheduler. Literature reports a 15 s global reconfiguration.

claims.claim: Fiber is about 1.5 times slower than vacuum, and a 12 GHz carrier has an 83.33 ps period.
claims.measured: Fiber slowdown {{metrics.latency.fiber_slowdown|.1f}}x; 1/12 GHz = {{metrics.latency.ku_12ghz_period_ps|.2f}} ps.
claims.notes: The 1.5x figure is a representative refractive-index value, not a measured fiber route.

claims.claim: A Gen2 mini is about 800 kg with a roughly 30 m array span and 116 m2 area; Gen1 was about 300 kg with an 8 m panel.
claims.measured: Not measured; no mass, area, or dimension telemetry in public TLEs.
claims.notes: Operator specification repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: The user terminal is an electronically steered phased array, not a mechanically tracked dish.
claims.measured: Not measured; no terminal teardown or beam-pattern data.
claims.notes: Hardware claim from the explainer.

claims.claim: Spacecraft use star trackers and many Linux computers, including 4,000+ computers across 60 Gen1 satellites.
claims.measured: Not measured; no onboard avionics data.
claims.notes: Company statement repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: Argon Hall thrusters provide about 170 mN with a sub-2.3 kg unit, about 2.5x Gen1 thrust and 1.5x efficiency; propellant moved from krypton to argon.
claims.measured: Not measured; no thruster telemetry in public TLEs.
claims.notes: 170 mN is about 17.3 g-force equivalent, below a typical 23 g AA cell; the comparison is arithmetic, the thruster specification is external.

claims.claim: A separate high-frequency gateway channel and improved antennas give about 4x the capacity of Gen1.
claims.measured: Not measured; no capacity or gateway-link telemetry.
claims.notes: Operator claim repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: The user link uses about 12 GHz and electronic steering on microsecond scales.
claims.measured: 12 GHz period {{metrics.latency.ku_12ghz_period_ps|.2f}} ps verified arithmetically; steering latency and array hardware were not measured.
claims.notes: The period follows from the stated carrier; the beam-steering speed is a hardware claim.

claims.claim: Doppler at 11.325 GHz stays near +/-230 kHz with rates below 5 kHz/s at a 25 deg mask.
claims.measured: p95 max Doppler {{metrics.service.median_doppler_p95_khz|.1f}} kHz (range {{metrics.service.doppler_p95_range_khz.0}}-{{metrics.service.doppler_p95_range_khz.1}}); p95 rate {{metrics.service.median_rate_p95_khz_s|.2f}} kHz/s (max {{metrics.service.rate_p95_max_khz_s|.2f}}); sites with p95 rate >5 kHz/s: {{metrics.service.frac_sites_rate_gt_5|pct}}.
claims.notes: Geometric Doppler, not a receiver implementation. The 230 kHz and 5 kHz/s figures are consistent with the cited measurements.

claims.claim: Laser links use three terminals per satellite at 100-200 Gbps; the mesh reportedly carries 260,000 links/day, spans 5,400 km, acquires in 12 s, and moves 42 PB/day at over 99% uptime.
claims.measured: Not measured; public TLEs carry no laser telemetry.
claims.notes: Company statements repeated by the explainer; not independently verified.

claims.claim: The network reconfigures on a roughly 15 s global schedule.
claims.measured: Geometric handover p50 {{metrics.service.median_handover_interval_s|.1f}} s (range {{metrics.service.handover_p50_range_s.0}}-{{metrics.service.handover_p50_range_s.1}}); no scheduler telemetry.
claims.notes: Our best-satellite simulation is consistent with 15 s slots but cannot prove the operational schedule.

claims.claim: Satellites are bent-pipe relays to gateways, and the US has more than 100 gateway sites.
claims.measured: Radio bounds are consistent with a bent-pipe path ({{metrics.service.median_rtt_lower_p50_ms|.2f}}-{{metrics.service.median_rtt_upper_p50_ms|.2f}} ms); the gateway count is external.
claims.notes: No gateway coordinates were used; the count is an operator claim.

claims.claim: Covering the globe from about 500 km requires thousands of satellites.
claims.measured: A {{metrics.service.meta.n_satellites|,}}-satellite simulation yields {{metrics.service.median_visible_p50|.1f}} visible p50 per site; no counterfactual small-constellation run.
claims.notes: Coverage geometry, not a market or capacity argument.

claims.claim: About 4,400 satellites moved from roughly 550 to 480 km in 2026.
claims.measured: Measured medians: 70 deg {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.70.alt_a_median_km|.1f}} -> {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.70.alt_b_median_km|.1f}} km (n={{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.70.matched|,}}, {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.70.frac_lowered_gt10km|pct}} lowered >10 km); 53.1 deg {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.53p1.alt_a_median_km|.1f}} -> {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.53p1.alt_b_median_km|.1f}} km (n={{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.53p1.matched|,}}); 43 deg stable at {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.43.alt_b_median_km|.1f}} km; 97.4 deg {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.97p4.alt_a_median_km|.1f}} -> {{metrics.migration.by_family.apr2026_nov2026.97p4.alt_b_median_km|.1f}} km.
claims.notes: The exact 4,400 count is external. The public '550 to 480' summary is shell-specific: 483, 463, 475, and 465 km in our data.

claims.claim: SpaceX conducted 165 launches in 2025.
claims.measured: Our SATCAT-derived count is {{metrics.launches.launches_2025}} Starlink-dedicated launches carrying {{metrics.launches.sats_2025|,}} still-on-orbit objects; total Falcon 9 launches cannot be separated from this table.
claims.notes: Different denominators: 165 is an all-launch company figure, while 122 counts Starlink launches inferred from on-orbit object IDs.

claims.claim: About 1,000 Starlink satellites launched in the first 3.5 months of 2026.
claims.measured: {{metrics.launches.first_3p5m_2026|,}} on-orbit objects with launch dates 2026-01-01 through 2026-04-15.
claims.notes: Counts surviving catalog objects, not all launched objects.

claims.claim: A Falcon 9 Starlink stack now carries 25-29 satellites.
claims.measured: 2025: median {{metrics.launches.per_launch.2025.median}} ({{metrics.launches.per_launch.2025.frac_25_to_29|pct}} in 25-29, n={{metrics.launches.per_launch.2025.n_launches}}); 2026: median {{metrics.launches.per_launch.2026.median}} ({{metrics.launches.per_launch.2026.frac_25_to_29|pct}}, n={{metrics.launches.per_launch.2026.n_launches}}).
claims.notes: The historical 21-satellite first Gen2 stack is not re-tested.

claims.claim: Starship V3 is about 2 t with over 1 Tbit/s; 20 satellites flew at about 190 km in July 2026; 26 operational satellites followed in late September 2026; future flights may carry 60.
claims.measured: November 2026 snapshot: {{metrics.v3_group.n}} objects at 30.5 deg, median {{metrics.v3_group.alt_median_km|.1f}} km; {{metrics.v3_group.launch_days.2026_09_28}} have a 2026-09-28 launch date at {{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_09_28.0|.1f}}-{{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_09_28.1|.1f}} km; {{metrics.v3_group.launch_days.2026_11_13}} have a 2026-11-13 date at {{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_11_13.0|.1f}}-{{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_11_13.1|.1f}} km. Mass and throughput were not measured.
claims.notes: The 26-satellite cohort is consistent with the first operational V3 launch; vehicle type, mass, and throughput remain external.

claims.claim: The 30.5 deg group is a fresh two-cohort deployment signature, not a long-lived operational shell.
claims.measured: {{metrics.v3_group.n}} objects at 30.5 deg: {{metrics.v3_group.launch_days.2026_09_28}} launched 2026-09-28 at {{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_09_28.0|.1f}}-{{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_09_28.1|.1f}} km; {{metrics.v3_group.launch_days.2026_11_13}} launched 2026-11-13 at {{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_11_13.0|.1f}}-{{metrics.v3_group.alt_range_by_day.2026_11_13.1|.1f}} km.
claims.notes: The second cohort is visibly raising through the first cohort's altitude, which explains the spread rather than a stable 345 km shell.

claims.claim: The catalog gained about 1,437 objects and lost 358 between April and November 2026.
claims.measured: {{metrics.population_flow.0.new|,}} new, {{metrics.population_flow.0.missing}} missing, {{metrics.population_flow.0.matched|,}} matched over {{metrics.population_flow.0.months|.2f}} months; identity check {{metrics.population_flow.0.check_identity}}.
claims.notes: Missing means absent from the later snapshot, not confirmed decayed; SATCAT retains only on-orbit objects.

claims.claim: Catalog attrition is about 0.46% per month, with about 187 new objects per month.
claims.measured: {{metrics.population_flow.0.missing_pct_per_month|.2f}}% missing per month; {{metrics.population_flow.0.new_per_month|.1f}} new per month.
claims.notes: Rates assume a constant process over the 7.69-month interval; they are descriptive, not a survival model.

claims.claim: Starlink performed more than 355,000 avoidance maneuvers from June 2025 to May 2026, over 40 per satellite per year, with a threshold 10 times lower than industry.
claims.measured: Not measured; our TLE panel detects {{metrics.maneuvers.events}} orbit-control steps in {{metrics.maneuvers.satellites}} satellites, which are not avoidance events.
claims.notes: The TLE-step count is a different quantity (altitude changes, not conjunction-driven maneuvers).

claims.claim: Drag shortens failed-satellite lifetime by more than 80% during solar minimum.
claims.measured: Not measured; no solar-cycle or drag model was run.
claims.notes: Company/regulatory statement repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: Lower satellites decay faster.
claims.measured: Linearized lifetimes: 30.5 deg {{metrics.decay_by_family.30p5.life_median_yr|.2f}} yr; 53.1 deg {{metrics.decay_by_family.53p1.life_median_yr|.2f}} yr; 43 deg {{metrics.decay_by_family.43.life_median_yr|.2f}} yr; 70 deg {{metrics.decay_by_family.70.life_median_yr|.2f}} yr; 97.4 deg {{metrics.decay_by_family.97p4.life_median_yr|.2f}} yr.
claims.notes: Derived from TLE ndot and a linearized altitude model; not a propagator lifetime and not a solar-cycle prediction.

claims.claim: Astronomy mitigation uses dark paint, mirror film, attitude changes, and published ephemerides.
claims.measured: Not measured; no brightness or observatory data.
claims.notes: Operational and policy claim repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: Direct-to-cell is a distinct sub-constellation intended to serve ordinary 4G phones.
claims.measured: {{metrics.dtc.n_nov2026}} DTC-tagged objects in November 2026; median altitude {{metrics.dtc.alt_median_nov2026_km|.1f}} km; inclination {{metrics.dtc.inc_median_2025_deg|.2f}} deg (Apr 2025) -> {{metrics.dtc.inc_median_2026_deg|.2f}} deg (Apr 2026) -> {{metrics.dtc.inc_median_nov2026_deg|.2f}} deg (Nov 2026).
claims.notes: The DTC tag is a name suffix, not a service test; the plane change is measured, the phone compatibility is external.

claims.claim: Six DTC satellites launched in January 2024 and the first text messages followed days later; the phone transmits at about 0.2 W.
claims.measured: Not measured; no launch or link-budget data.
claims.notes: Company statement repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: DTC service operates with carriers in the US, Canada, Japan, and Australia and uses laser backhaul.
claims.measured: Not measured; no carrier or backhaul telemetry.
claims.notes: Operator claim repeated by the explainer.

claims.claim: The SGP4 implementation matches the official verification vectors.
claims.measured: {{metrics.sgp4_validation.vectors_compared}} vectors across {{metrics.sgp4_validation.cases_with_vectors}} cases; {{metrics.sgp4_validation.propagation_errors}} declared propagation error; max position error {{metrics.sgp4_validation.max_pos_km}} km.
claims.notes: Python sgp4 2.27 against SGP4-VER.TLE/tcppver.out.

claims.claim: J2 nodal regression predicts RAAN to better than 0.1% at the median.
claims.measured: Median |relative error| {{metrics.j2.median_abs_rel_error_pct|.3f}}%, p95 {{metrics.j2.p95_abs_rel_error_pct|.3f}}%, max {{metrics.j2.max_abs_rel_error_pct|.3f}}% over {{metrics.j2.n_satellites}} satellites.
claims.notes: A 27-satellite, 17-month TLE panel; residual spread is bimodal and not fully explained.

claims.claim: TLE mean-motion altitudes agree with SATCAT to about 1 km.
claims.measured: n={{metrics.satcat_altitude_check.n|,}}; median |difference| {{metrics.satcat_altitude_check.median_abs_diff_km|.2f}} km, p95 {{metrics.satcat_altitude_check.p95_abs_diff_km|.2f}} km, p99 {{metrics.satcat_altitude_check.p99_abs_diff_km|.2f}} km, max {{metrics.satcat_altitude_check.max_abs_diff_km|.2f}} km.
claims.notes: SATCAT apogee/perigee midpoint versus TLE semi-major-axis altitude; the tail includes eccentric or maneuvering objects.

claims.claim: Plane counts are stable at a 0.2 deg RAAN threshold.
claims.measured: 43 deg / 483 km: {{metrics.planes.by_key.43_483.planes}} groups; 53.1 deg / 463 km: {{metrics.planes.by_key.53p1_463.planes}}; 70 deg / 475 km: {{metrics.planes.by_key.70_475.planes}}; 97.4 deg / 465 km: {{metrics.planes.by_key.97p4_465.planes}}.
claims.notes: The full threshold sensitivity table is results/tables/anatomy_stability_nov2026.csv; 0.05 deg is degenerate because group RAAN standard deviation is about 0.2 deg.
